_readme: Hand-curated non-HDB training venues. HDB blocks are NOT listed here — they are
generated into public/data/venues.json by scripts/ingest_hdb.py from data.gov.sg.
IMPORTANT: the coordinates and elevations below are SEED VALUES. They are
approximate and every one of them is marked elevationSource: 'estimated'.
Correcting them is the single most useful first contribution to this project —
see CONTRIBUTING.md. When you verify a figure against a real source, update the
value, set elevationSource to 'verified', and cite the source in 'notes'.
summitM = height above sea level at the top.
gainM   = elevation actually climbed from the usual start point. This is the
number that matters for training and is often much smaller than
summitM: Bukit Timah tops out around 163 m but the visitor centre is

venues.name: Bukit Timah Hill
venues.notes: Highest natural point in Singapore. Summit figure is widely cited as ~163 m and is the one value here worth trusting; gain from the visitor centre still needs measuring. Nature reserve — check opening hours and closure days.

venues.name: Mount Faber
venues.notes: Frequently cited around 105 m but unconfirmed here. Reached by road or by the Marang Trail steps. Anchor of the Southern Ridges.

venues.name: Marang Trail
venues.notes: Continuous stepped ascent from near HarbourFront up to Mount Faber. Popular repeat-climb venue. Step count and gain both need measuring.

venues.name: Telok Blangah Hill Park
venues.notes: Links to Mount Faber via Henderson Waves and to Kent Ridge via the Forest Walk.

venues.name: Kent Ridge Park
venues.notes: Western end of the Southern Ridges. Canopy Walk plus a stepped climb from Pepys Road.

venues.name: Bukit Gombak
venues.notes: Access is partly restricted — confirm which paths are public before adding routes.

venues.name: Fort Canning Hill
venues.notes: Small central hill, often quoted near 48 m. Several stepped approaches — the Fort Canning Centre steps are the steepest. Useful for city-centre repeats.

venues.name: Pearl's Hill City Park
venues.notes: Small, central, quiet. Short stepped climb from Chin Swee Road.

venues.name: Mount Emily Park
venues.notes: Very small central rise; listed mainly for completeness of the city-centre set.
